note.question: Do start-ups adopt worker-centered cultures to improve productivity or to attract employees at lower wages?
note.overview: Workers choose employers based on wage and culture, entrepreneurs choose culture to maximize profit, and a unique wage differential clears both labor-market segments.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

components.label: Unique competitive labor-market sorting equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique competitive labor-market sorting equilibrium. Section 6.1.3, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 11), defines equilibrium by worker utility maximization, entrepreneur profit maximization, and market clearing. Equation (4) equates worker supply and firm demand and has a unique wage differential.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Given the relative wage across culture types, workers choose the culture that maximizes wage plus culture utility and entrepreneurs choose the culture that maximizes productivity net of wages. The relative wage adjusts until labor supply equals labor demand for each culture. Workers sort by their utility value for culture. Entrepreneurs sort by culture-specific productivity effects.
